 Prayer:

Civil Miscellaneous Appeal filed under Section 173  Vehicles Act, 1988, against the judgment and decree dated 25.04.201  MCOP No. 131 of 2016 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Trib  II Additional District and Sessions Court, Chidambaram.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Trib  II Additional District and Sessions Court, Chidambaram
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: For Appellant : Mrs.N.R.Surekha  For Respondents : Mr. N.Somasundar R6  RR1 to 4, 5, 9  No appeara  RR7 and 8 No ready notice  JUDGMENT

This appellant/Insurance Company has come forward with this appeal seeking reduction of compensation in the judgment and decree dated 25.04.2018, in MCOP No. 131 of 2016 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, II Additional District and Sessions Court, Chidambaram.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, II Additional District and Sessions Court, Chidambaram
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. It is the case of the appellant that on 25.05.2016 while the deceased, aged about 30 years, was driving his lorry bearing Registration No. TN 18 9984 from Chennai to Madurai because of the oncoming dazzling head lights, he drove the vehicle towards left hand side without danger lights signaling the parking of the vehicle, the deceased has hit the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis stationed lorry from behind and due to the accident, he died.

Thereafter, the claimants, who are the wife and children of the deceased, has filed a Claim Petition before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, claiming Rs.50,00,000/- as compensation under various heads.
3. During the trial before the Tribunal, on the side of the claimant, two witnesses were examined and and marked four documents viz., Exs.P1 to P18.
On the side of the respondents, no witness was examined and no document was marked.
4. The Tribunal, considering the oral and documentary evidence, allowed the petition in part and awarded a sum of Rs.21,52,800/- as compensation to the claimants.
Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation, the appellant insurance company has filed this appeal before this Court.

5. The learned counsel for the appellant/Insurance company submitted that before the Tribunal, the appellant had filed a detailed counter contending that the accident had taken place only due to the negligence of the deceased and it was specifically stated in the FIR and charge sheet were https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis registered that the deceased alone driven the lorry in a rash and negligence manner and caused the accident.
Further, the age, avocation and income of the deceased has not been proved before the Tribunal.
Without considering these facts, the Tribunal has awarded compensation to the claimants, which is highly excessive and the same is erroneous.
6. The learned counsel for the respondents/claimants submitted that admittedly, the accident had happened in the National Highways.
As per the National Highways Rules, the places were earmarked for parking the vehicle.

In the present case, the lorry owned by the 7 th respondent and insured with the appellant, which was break downed and stationed without any parking lamp,
The Manager vs Jayapradha on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31434595/
2 parked at the left side of the National Highways Road and the said lorry was loaded by the iron road without any caution.

Due to the accident the projected steel rods which were loaded in the 7th respondent's lorry, pierced the front portion of the 5th respondent's lorry and its driver deceased Prakash succumbed to his injuries and died on the spot.
Therefore, the Tribunal has fixed entire negligence on the lorry owned by the 5th respondent and its insurer, which is perfectly in order and the same does not warrant any interference.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 7.
Heard both sides and perused the materials available on record.
8. The factum of the accident is not disputed by the parties and he appeal has been filed on the ground of negligence and liability.
On perusal of the award, it is found that the 7 th respondents lorry was stationed on the left side of the road due to mechanical fault.
However, on perusal of the Motor Vehicle Inspection report, there is no mechanical defect found in the lorry and the Motor Vehicle Inspection has not examined before the Tribunal.
It is clear that the 7th respondent's lorry was parked at no parking area without any indication.
Therefore, the Tribunal has fixed entire negligence on the part of the driver of the 7th respondent lorry and hence, the appellant, who is its insurer, is liable to pay compensation.
The finding of the Tribunal is perfectly in order and the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable and hence, the same does not require any interference.
9. In view of the above, this Court do not find any error in the award passed by the Tribunal.
There is no merit in the appeal.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 10
. In the result, the Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is dismissed.

The appellant insurance company is directed to deposit the entire amount awarded by the Tribunal along with interest at 7.5%, less the amount already deposited if any, within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.

On such deposit being made, the claimants shall withdraw the compensation as awarded by the Tribunal along with interest and costs, less the amount, if any, already withdrawn,
by filing an appropriate application before the Court concerned.
No costs.
